lines: Stream's yours again today. You good?
One sentence.
And the overflow room?
Online gets the service. The overflow room gets the stream on the TV, a little behind — and I'll tell them why.
Nobody's watching “a stream.” They're watching us.
What broke, what almost broke, what do we fix before next week?
Unknown. The evidence went when I restarted the switch. That one's mine.
Guest speaker next Sunday. She's bringing her own laptop.
Maya, meet our speaker. She has a video with sound at the sermon.
Andre can come Tuesday to look at the stage circuits. He's bringing his apprentice.
Yes, do the rack. Thanks, Mateo. Theo, tell Maya it's happening.
We found it. A cable moved on Tuesday. We may start two minutes late. That one's on my process.
The breaker's in the electrical room, right? Can we just flip it back on?
And it's not our room.
Put it on my list.
Then we ask. Every month.
Christmas Eve planning starts now. Lena from the broadcast studio is coming to look at our cameras.
It's only rented through January. Lena runs cameras for a living.
The board meets on the fourteenth. Tasha wants a list of everything that could break — and what it costs if we do nothing.
UPS: me, review in April. Documentation: Ray and Maya, before summer.
It happened, Tasha. Five minutes, room and stream. The card worked — except the password.
Tasha says: UPS goes on April's agenda, first item. And: “Tell Maya she was right to say she didn't know.”
